title: Constant-coefficient tensor calculus for the finite etale exceptional adjoint
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$, let $\ell\ne p$ be prime, and let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism of finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. No separatedness of $Y$ over $k$ is assumed. Fix a compactification $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p_f}Y$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Let $C$ be a finite commutative ring annihilated by a power of $\ell$. Use the ordinary unbounded etale derived categories $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},C)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], put $F_{f,C}=Rp_{f,*}j_!$, and fix its right adjoint $G_{f,C}$ with counit $\epsilon_C$ [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. There exists an integer $N_f\ge0$ depending only on $f$, not on $C$, such that, for every integer $a$, $F_{f,C}$ sends $D^{\le a}$ into $D^{\le a+N_f}$, using the standard cohomological bounds [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. For any integer $d\ge0$ bounding the dimensions of all geometric fibres of $f$, one can take $N_f=2d$.

For $V\in D(C\text{-}\mathrm{Mod})$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], write $V_T$ for the termwise constant-sheaf complex on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and use derived tensor as in [def-kun-derived-tensor]; no boundedness or perfectness of $V$ is imposed. For every $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},C)$ and $M\in D(Y_{\mathrm{et}},C)$, the canonical maps
$$V_Y\otimes_C^L F_{f,C}K\longrightarrow F_{f,C}(V_X\otimes_C^L K),\qquad V_X\otimes_C^L G_{f,C}M\longrightarrow G_{f,C}(V_Y\otimes_C^L M)$$
are isomorphisms. The first is the compact-support projection map. The second is its adjunction transpose: its transpose is the composite
$$F_{f,C}(V_X\otimes_C^LG_{f,C}M)\xrightarrow{\mathrm{proj}^{-1}}V_Y\otimes_C^LF_{f,C}G_{f,C}M\xrightarrow{1\otimes\epsilon_C}V_Y\otimes_C^LM.$$
These are natural transformations on the unbounded derived categories and independent of complex resolutions. The tensor here is by a constant coefficient complex $V$; no analogous assertion for an arbitrary sheaf complex on $Y$ is included.

proof.text: Apply the unbounded-amplitude lemma to the fixed compactification. It supplies a geometric fibre bound $d$ depending only on $f$ and gives $F(D^{\le a})\subset D^{\le a+2d}$ for every such bound. Set $N_f=2d$; this proves the coefficient-uniform assertion and its explicit bound, including empty schemes.

proof.text: Use the coherent unital shift-compatible support projection isomorphism, restricted along the termwise constant functor on Y. Its target is the action V ↦ f*V_Y ⊗ K followed by F. Retain this action for the generation argument. The inverse symmetric braiding is the swapped forward braiding. Naturality of the final symmetry shows that postcomposing this projection by F of tensor applied to exceptionalConstantPullbackIso gives exactly exceptionalConstantProjectionMap.

source.place: Theorem 2.18(2), Corollary 2.19 (printed p. 12), Construction 2.26 and Proposition 2.29(2) (printed pp. 14–16), specialized to schemes over Spec k. Supplies the finite-coefficient tensor input to the adic-stage paragraph of def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image.

proof.text: The amplitude and projection assertions just obtained are exactly the hypotheses of the compact-image/adjoint-coproduct lemma, with $N=2d$. Apply it to the fixed adjunction $F\dashv G$. It gives an exact shift structure on $G$ and its explicit counit compatibility equation. Derive unit compatibility from that equation by cancelling the inverse shift comparison, transposing under the adjunction, and applying naturality and the triangle identity. Thus the fixed adjunction commutes with shifts. It also supplies, for every $M$ exact coproduct-preserving functors $A_M(V)=V_X\otimes_C^L GM$ and $B_M(V)=G(V_Y\otimes_C^L M)$.

source.place: Theorem 2.18(2), Corollary 2.19 (printed p. 12), Construction 2.26 and Proposition 2.29(2) (printed pp. 14–16), specialized to schemes over Spec k. Supplies the finite-coefficient tensor input to the adic-stage paragraph of def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image.

proof.text: Apply coefficientActionAdjointGeneration with source action TA(K)(V)=f*V_Y ⊗ K and target action TB(M)(V)=V_Y ⊗ M. Constant sheaves, exact pullback, and derived tensor are triangulated with their canonical shifts; their composites preserve coproducts, and the compact-image lemma gives coproduct preservation of G. Restriction of the coherent support projection gives Q. Its shift equation follows from projection naturality along the constant functor shift comparison and the coherent support projection shift equation. Identify the single free rank-one ULift C module with the coefficient tensor unit through ULift.moduleEquiv. The action unit is the constant unit followed on X by the pullback unit; naturality in that coefficient isomorphism and the coherent projection unit equation prove the hypothesis at the generator. The generation theorem gives the naturality equations and invertibility for every coefficient complex; its internal proof uses generating-class determination and derived-module free generation, retaining that route. Assemble these equations by NatIso.ofComponents into AQ. Now transport TA to the specified constant-coefficient action by the natural isomorphism b induced by exceptionalConstantPullbackIso. Set P=Q followed by F of b, and A=b⁻¹ at GM followed by AQ. Tensor symmetry naturality proves the required formula for P. Naturality of adj.homEquiv in its source proves that A is exactly the counit mate specified in the item. All proof helpers and equations are proved privately. The public projection map and its characterization use the same real generic constructor for the original canonical composite; existing statements and maps are unchanged, and no new holes are introduced.
